title: Dependency audit 2026-08-20: react-router RCE fix + upgrade plan & instruction set
description:
# Dependency audit — 2026-08-20

Branch: `dependency-upgrades` · Tooling: bun 1.3.14 · Sources: `bun outdated`, `bun audit`, lockfile inspection across root + workspaces (front-end, back-end, shared).

## 1. Security findings

`bun audit`: **52 vulnerabilities (26 high, 22 moderate, 4 low)**.

### 1a. Direct dep with published same-major fix — do first

**react-router 7.13.0 → ≥7.14.2** (front-end dependency, exact pin; vulnerable range `>=7.0.0 <=7.14.1`, 11 advisories):

- GHSA-49rj-9fvp-4h2h (high): Unauth RCE — vendored turbo-stream v2 allows arbitrary constructor invocation via TYPE_ERROR deserialization
- GHSA-8646-j5j9-6r62 (high): XSS via `javascript:` targets in unstable RSC redirect handling
- GHSA-8x6r-g9mw-2r78 (high): DoS via unbounded path expansion in `__manifest`
- GHSA-rxv8-25v2-qmq8 (high): DoS via reflected user input in single-fetch
- GHSA-chx6-hx7r-mcp5 (high): Unauth DoS via inefficient route matching
- GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2 (high): RSC mode CSRF bypass (action executed before 400)
- Moderate/low: stored XSS via unescaped Location header, open redirect via `\` in Link/useNavigate (CVE-2025-68470 bypass), protocol-relative `//` open redirect, RSCErrorHandler XSS, arbitrary constructor injection via `deserializeErrors()`, CSRF via PUT/PATCH/DELETE

### 1b. Transitive advisories (fix via `bun update` and/or parent upgrades)

| Package (locked) | Worst severity + advisory | Path | Fix available? |
|---|---|---|---|
| vite 7.3.3 | high: GHSA-fx2h-pf6j-xcff (`server.fs.deny` bypass, Windows); moderate: GHSA-v6wh-96g9-6wx3 (launch-editor NTLMv2) | front-end dev | Needs >7.3.4 — check registry for a 7.x patch; if none, vite 8 = major (separate task) |
| find-my-way 9.6.0 | high: GHSA-c96f-x56v-gq3h (HTTP2 DDoS) | back-end › fastify 5.8.5 | Needs >9.6.0 — check fastify 5.x releases; else fastify 6 = major (separate task) |
| js-yaml 3.14.2 | high: GHSA-52cp-r559-cp3m, CVE-2026-59870 (quadratic CPU); moderate: GHSA-h67p-54hq-rp68 | back-end › gray-matter 4.0.3; front-end › shadcn | `bun update` → 3.15.x fixes some; CVE-2026-59870 not backported to 3.x → needs js-yaml 4 or gray-matter replacement (approval required) |
| brace-expansion 1.1.15 | high: GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg, GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895, GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp (DoS) | serve 14.2.6 › serve-handler › minimatch 3.1.5 | Needs >1.1.17; minimatch 3.1.5 allows `^1.1.7` — `bun update` should resolve |
| hono 4.12.23 | high: GHSA-88fw-hqm2-52qc (CORS reflects any Origin with credentials) + 5 moderate | front-end › shadcn (dev CLI) | Needs ≥4.12.34 — `bun update` |
| @hono/node-server 1.19.14 | moderate: GHSA-frvp-7c67-39w9 (path traversal, Windows) | front-end › shadcn | Needs ≥1.19.15 — `bun update` |
| ip-address 10.2.0 | high: GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr (SSRF/trust-boundary bypass) + 2 moderate | front-end › shadcn | Needs >10.3.0 — `bun update` / shadcn 4 |
| nanoid 3.3.12 | high: GHSA-28wg-ghj8-5hjv, GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8 (infinite loops) | front-end › shadcn, vite | Needs ≥3.3.16 — `bun update` |
| postcss 8.5.15 | high: GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849 (source-map path traversal) + moderate GHSA-fxqj-rqcc-2cmp | front-end › shadcn, vite | Needs >8.5.22 — `bun update` |
| fast-uri 3.1.2 | high: GHSA-4c8g-83qw-93j6 (IDN host confusion) | shadcn/hono stack | Needs ≥3.1.5 — `bun update` |
| esbuild 0.27.7 | low: GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr (dev-server file read, Windows) | front-end › vite | Needs ≥0.28.1 — `bun update` (dev-only exposure) |
| body-parser 2.2.2 | low: GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6 (limit DoS) | front-end › shadcn | Needs ≥2.3.0 — `bun update` |

**Risk note:** shadcn/hono/ip-address/nanoid/postcss transitive deps sit behind a dev-time CLI that is never bundled into the shipped site → low practical exposure, but bump the lockfile entries anyway. **Runtime-facing exposure: react-router (front-end), vite (front-end dev server), find-my-way + js-yaml (back-end).**

## 2. In-range updates available (`bun outdated`)

| Package | Location | Range style | Locked | Target |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| react-router | front-end dep | exact | 7.13.0 | latest 7.x ≥ 7.14.2 (security) |
| @playwright/test | root dev | exact | 1.56.0 | 1.62.1 |
| eslint | root dev | ^ | 10.4.1 | 10.8.1 |
| typescript-eslint | root dev | ^ | 8.60.0 | 8.67.0 |
| @eslint/js | root dev | ^ | 9.39.4 | 9.39.5 |

All other workspace direct deps are current within their ranges.

## 3. Major-only upgrades (per AGENTS.md: each is its own task/PR — NOT part of this ticket)

- **typescript 5.9.3 → 7.0.2** (root dev). Blocker to check first: typescript-eslint 8.60.0 peer range is `typescript >=4.8.4 <6.1.0` — verify a tse release supporting TS 7 exists before planning.
- **shadcn 3.8.5 → 4.18.0** (root + front-end dev). Likely pulls newer hono/ip-address/nanoid/postcss transitives; review CLI breaking changes.
- **@eslint/js 9.39.5 → 10.0.1** (root dev). Aligns with eslint 10.x already in use.
- **vite 7 → 8** (only if no 7.x security patch exists).
- **fastify 5 → 6** (only if no 5.x ships find-my-way >9.6.0).
- **gray-matter**: replace or accept residual js-yaml 3.x CVE-2026-59870.

## Instruction set

### Phase 0 — prep
1. Claim this ticket: `bd update <id> --claim`
2. Work on branch `dependency-upgrades` (already created from main).

### Phase 1 — react-router security fix (own commit, do first)
1. Confirm the fixed version: `npm view react-router@7 versions --json | tail -5` and check the GHSA-49rj-9fvp-4h2h advisory page for the patched version. Target: latest 7.x ≥ 7.14.2.
2. Keep the exact-pin style: `cd front-end && bun add react-router@<7.x.y>` (bun resolves the workspace automatically).
3. `cd .. && bun install` (sync lockfile) — verify `bun.lock` now pins the new react-router.
4. Gates (router is core — full e2e mandatory):
   - `bun run lint && bun run typecheck && bun test`
   - `docker compose up -d` → `bun run test:e2e` → `docker compose down`
5. Commit: `chore(deps): bump react-router to <7.x.y> (fix GHSA-49rj-9fvp-4h2h et al.)`

### Phase 2 — remaining in-range direct updates (single commit)
From repo root, explicit versions matching existing range style:
1. `bun add -d @playwright/test@1.62.1` (exact pin — keep style)
2. `bun add -d eslint@^10.8.1`
3. `bun add -d @eslint/js@^9.39.5`
4. `bun add -d typescript-eslint@^8.67.0`
5. `bun update` — bumps transitives within existing ranges (expected: brace-expansion 1.1.17+, hono ≥4.12.34, nanoid ≥3.3.16, postcss >8.5.22, js-yaml 3.15.x, fast-uri ≥3.1.5, body-parser ≥2.3.0, @hono/node-server ≥1.19.15, esbuild ≥0.28.1 if vite-compatible).
6. Verify: `bun outdated` shows no remaining in-range updates; `bun audit` before/after counts recorded in a ticket comment (`bd comment <id> ...`).
7. Gates: `bun run lint && bun run typecheck && bun test` + e2e (docker compose up → `bun run test:e2e` → down).
8. Commit: `chore(deps): bump eslint, @eslint/js, typescript-eslint, @playwright/test within major`
   (package.json + bun.lock committed together.)

### Phase 3 — verify transitive advisory resolution
1. `bun audit` — for each remaining advisory, classify and record in a ticket comment:
   - (a) resolved by Phase 1/2,
   - (b) requires a parent major → file a follow-up task (see Phase 4 list),
   - (c) accepted risk with written rationale (dev-only tooling exposure).
2. Do not close this ticket while any runtime-facing high advisory (react-router, vite, find-my-way, js-yaml) is unaddressed without an approved follow-up ticket.

### Phase 4 — file follow-up tickets for major upgrades (one task each, separate PRs)
1. typescript 5 → 7 (verify tse peer support first)
2. shadcn 3 → 4 (root + front-end)
3. @eslint/js 9 → 10
4. vite 7 → 8 (if no 7.x security patch) — check @vitejs/plugin-react + @tailwindcss/vite peer ranges
5. fastify 5 → 6 (if no 5.x ships find-my-way >9.6.0)
6. gray-matter: replace vs accept residual CVE-2026-59870

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] react-router ≥ 7.14.2 in front-end/package.json + bun.lock
- [ ] `bun outdated` shows no remaining in-range updates
- [ ] `bun audit` before/after recorded in ticket comments; all runtime-facing high advisories fixed or have approved follow-up tickets
- [ ] `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun test` all pass
- [ ] E2E passes (docker compose up → `bun run test:e2e` → down)
- [ ] package.json + bun.lock committed together, Conventional Commits
- [ ] Pushed per AGENTS.md session protocol; `.beads/issues.jsonl` synced with `chore(beads): sync issue tracker` if pending

## Rules (AGENTS.md — dependency management)
- Explicit version on every install; match existing range style (caret vs exact pin)
- Never `--force` / `--legacy-peer-deps`; report conflicts instead
- No major upgrades as side-effects of this ticket
- Lockfile only via bun; lockfile committed alongside package.json
- Get user approval before each package change (state package, version, reason)

title: Container workflow migration to pure Podman + Cloudflare Tunnel (decision record)
description:
## Purpose
Retire docker-compose and any Docker binary dependency; move local dev, CI, and single-host deployment to a pure-Podman workflow (`podman kube play`) with Cloudflare Tunnel for exposure. This issue is the permanent decision record.

## Decisions (reviewed and agreed)
| Area | Decision |
|---|---|
| Topology | Single physical host |
| App mechanism | `podman kube play` everywhere; `docker-compose.yml` retires |
| Declarative format | Checked-in Kube YAML (dev manifest + prod manifest) |
| Registry | GHCR, **public** images (repo itself is private; visibility is independent) |
| Tags / cadence | `:git-sha` (immutable) + `:latest` (advances only after green tests); 5-min pull timer |
| Content | Baked into prod image; CI guard fails release on any `draft: true` |
| Exposure | Cloudflare Tunnel (no inbound ports); no reverse proxy at origin (Cloudflare ingress) |
| TLS | Cloudflare edge only; origin is plain HTTP |
| cloudflared | Rootless Quadlet, token via host `0600` env file |
| Routing | Fastify mounts JSON API under `/api`; `/health` and `/content-assets/*` stay at root |
| Deploy | Pull-timer: `podman pull` + restart `podman-kube@website`; no CI-to-server credentials |
| Local dev | Thin `scripts/dev.sh` wrapper |

## Key assumptions
1. `/health` stays at root (kube readiness/liveness, CI wait loop, README target it) — only `/hello`, `/`, `/content`, `/content/:slug` move under `/api`.
2. `/content-assets/images/*` stays root (static asset path, not an API call) — `registerContentRoutes` is split in two.
3. Cloudflare Tunnel makes the origin see every client as localhost, so the rate limiter and `request.ip` must key on `CF-Connecting-IP`, trusted only from the tunnel.
4. Exactly one Quadlet (`cloudflared.container`) runs alongside the app kube manifest (infra-quadlet + app-kube-play).

## Sub-issues
- #260 — kube play manifests (dev + prod)
- #261 — Cloudflare Tunnel Quadlet + ingress
- #262 — systemd update pull-timer
- #263 — pin oven/bun images
- #264 — /api mount + drop proxy rewriting
- #265 — Cloudflare-aware rate limiting
- #266 — migrate container tests off docker-compose
- #267 — local dev scripts
- #268 — CI rewrite (GHCR publish, kube-play e2e, draft guard)
- #269 — server bootstrap runbook

## Phase order
1. Manifests + bun pin (#260, #263)
2. /api refactor + trust-proxy + tests + dev scripts (#264, #265, #266, #267)
3. CI rewrite (#268)
4. Server readdish + runbook (#262, #269, #261)

## Definition of done
- `docker-compose.yml` gone; local dev + CI e2e + prod all driven by `podman kube play`.
- GHCR publishes sha + latest tags; server self-updates via timer.
- Cloudflare Tunnel terminates TLS + mitigates bots; origin serves plain HTTP.
- No secrets in repo/images; only host-side tunnel token.

title: Make Fastify rate limiting Cloudflare-Tunnel-aware
description:
## Context
Behind Cloudflare Tunnel, cloudflared terminates at `127.0.0.1`, so the origin sees localhost/Cloudflare as the source IP for every client. The existing rate limiter would throttle all traffic as one client unless it keys on Cloudflare's `CF-Connecting-IP` header.

## Decision
- Enable Fastify `trustProxy` so proxied client metadata is honored only from the local tunnel (127.0.0.1).
- Configure the rate limiter's key generator to use `CF-Connecting-IP` (fallback to socket IP) so per-client limits apply.
- Verify Cloudflare's actual forwarded-header semantics (`CF-Connecting-IP`, `X-Forwarded-For`) during implementation; trust these only from localhost/cloudflared, never from arbitrary callers.

## Scope
- `back-end/src/core/rate-limit.ts`, `back-end/src/index.ts` / `app.ts` (trust proxy config).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Distinct `CF-Connecting-IP` values produce distinct rate-limit keys (no shared throttle).
- [ ] Direct (non-tunnel) requests cannot spoof client identity via headers.
- [ ] Tests cover spoofed-header attempts and tunnel-forwarded identities.

## Dependencies
Depends on: /api mount (same file area).

title: Mount JSON API under /api and drop proxy path-rewriting
description:
## Context
The back-end registers routes at root (`/content`, `/hello`, `/`). The `/api` prefix lives only in the front-end client (`api.ts` prepends `API_BASE`) and Vite's dev proxy, which strips it. Prod has no proxy, so `/api` is currently unstripped and unroutable. We make the back-end serve `/api/*` directly and remove all stripping.

## Decision
- `back-end/src/app.ts`: register hello/root/content-JSON routes inside a Fastify plugin scoped with `prefix: API_BASE` (`/api`).
- Split `registerContentRoutes`: JSON routes (`/content`, `/content/:slug`) under `/api`; the image route `/content-assets/images/*` stays at root (static asset path, not an API call).
- Keep `/health` at root (probe endpoint; kube probes, CI wait loop, and README all target it).
- `front-end/vite.config.ts`: remove the `/api` `rewrite`; forward `/api/*` unchanged so dev path == prod path.

## Scope
- `back-end/src/app.ts`, `back-end/src/features/content/content-routes.ts`, `front-end/vite.config.ts`.
- Update back-end route tests.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `/api/content`, `/api/content/:slug`, `/api/hello` respond on back-end.
- [ ] `/health` and `/content-assets/images/*` still respond at root.
- [ ] Vite dev proxy forwards `/api/*` transparently (no strip); front-end still works in dev.
- [ ] Existing back-end route tests updated and green.

## Dependencies
Unblocks: CI e2e, cloudflared ingress (no strip needed).

title: Add systemd pull-timer for image updates (pull :latest + replay kube pod)

title: Deploy Cloudflare Tunnel via rootless Quadlet + ingress config
description:
## Context
The site will be exposed via Cloudflare Tunnel (no inbound ports) rather than port-forwarding, for bot-traffic mitigation and edge TLS. There is no reverse proxy at origin; routing lives in cloudflared ingress.

## Decision
- `deploy/cloudflared/config.yml` — ingress rules (checked in, no secret):
  - `/api/*` and `/content-assets/*` -> `http://localhost:3001`
  - everything else -> `http://localhost:3000`
- `deploy/cloudflared/cloudflared.container` — rootless Quadlet running `docker.io/cloudflare/cloudflared`, token injected via `EnvironmentFile` (host-only `0600`), `AutoUpdate=registry`.

## Scope
- Add `deploy/cloudflared/config.yml`, `deploy/cloudflared/cloudflared.container`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Quadlet runs and establishes the outbound tunnel; token lives only in a host-side `0600` env file (never in repo/image).
- [ ] Ingress routes `/api/*` + `/content-assets/*` to back-end, all else to front-end.
- [ ] No TLS/ACME at origin (Cloudflare terminates TLS at the edge).

## Dependencies
Depends on: kube play manifests (ports 3000/3001).

title: Add podman kube play manifests (dev + prod), retire docker-compose.yml
description:
## Context
Local dev is currently orchestrated with `docker-compose.yml`, run via `podman compose` (which delegates to an external docker-compose binary). We are moving to a pure-Podman workflow where `podman kube play` is the single declarative format.

## Decision
Replace `docker-compose.yml` with two checked-in Kube manifests:
- `deploy/kube/dev.yaml` — pod `website`: front-end + back-end DEV images, hostPath bind mounts, HMR/watch, ports 5173/3001.
- `deploy/kube/prod.yaml` — same pod: PROD images `ghcr.io/tim-van-oudheusden/website/{front-end,back-end}:latest`, baked content (no host content mount), ports 3000/3001.

Generate a baseline with `podman generate kube`, then hand-tune (SELinux relabel on hostPath, health/readiness probes).

## Scope
- Add `deploy/kube/dev.yaml`, `deploy/kube/prod.yaml`.
- Delete `docker-compose.yml`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `podman kube play deploy/kube/dev.yaml` starts front-end (5173) + back-end (3001) with live reload over bind-mounted source.
- [ ] `podman kube play deploy/kube/prod.yaml` starts prod images; `/health` and `/` respond; content served from the baked image.
- [ ] `docker-compose.yml` removed.

## Dependencies
Unblocks: cloudflared ingress, CI e2e, server deploy.

title: Research: turn architecture review findings into implementation plans
description:
# Goal

The architecture review of 2026-09-29 (report: `/tmp/architecture-review-20260929-130926.html`) identified five deepening opportunities. **This ticket's goal: transform each finding into a concrete implementation plan.** No implementation code in this ticket — the deliverable is the plans themselves (record in the issue's design field or a `docs/` file, one section per candidate).

Each plan must contain: (1) target interface, (2) TDD steps (failing test → implementation → refactor, per repo rules), (3) files changed / deleted, (4) tests written first, (5) open decisions with a recommendation and rationale.

## Candidate 1 — Collapse the article document module (Strong)

**Finding:** The TOC-anchor-id invariant is held by two independent extraction pipelines that must agree: `extractMarkdownHeadings` (`front-end/src/shared/lib/markdown-headings.ts`, regex + fence tracking, count-based dedup `slug-1`, `slug-2`) and `extractMarkdownHeadingsWithOffsets` (`front-end/src/shared/components/MarkdownRenderer.tsx:120-156`, AST, offset lookup, fallback `slug-LINE-COLUMN` with no counter). `maxDepth=3` hardcoded in both. Only guard: `ArticlesPage.toc-consistency.test.ts` (filesystem-coupled, duplicates `stripFrontmatter` at lines 9-20). `ArticlePage.tsx` (120 lines) is dead: unrouted (App.tsx maps `/articles/:slug` → ArticlesPage), referenced only by its tautological test. TOC functions (`extractArticleTableOfContents`, `navigateToArticleHeadingById` with 4-fn `TocNavigationDependencies`, `resolveActiveTocHeadingIds`) are exported from the 537-line page; `resolveArticlesTrailTargetSlug` (107-109) is a one-line pass-through to `getDefaultArticleSlug`.

**Plan must decide:** target interface (proposed `renderArticle(markdown) → { html, toc }`); which heading-id scheme becomes the single source (count-based vs offset); module location (`shared/lib` vs `features/articles`); where TOC navigation + active-heading logic goes; which tests survive (the cross-module consistency test should become deletable — the invariant becomes structural); deletion of dead `ArticlePage.tsx` + its test.

## Candidate 2 — Deepen the content normalization seam (Strong)

**Finding:** `normalizeFrontmatter` (`back-end/src/features/content/content.ts:104-185`) silently drops invalid values: `content/Minimal Android Launcher.md:15` has `status: In development`, not in `PROJECT_STATUSES` — badge never renders, no error, no test. `prioritySlot` is declared in `shared/src/index.ts:109` and consumed by `project-display.ts:22-37` but `normalizeFrontmatter` never emits it (front-end tests pass on hand-built fixtures). `type` is hardcoded at `content.ts:131`, duplicating `CONTENT_TYPES`. `socialImage` appears in 4 content files but is absent from the contract and never read. Normalizer is private, exercised only via `content.real.test.ts` (asserts `items.length >= 8` + 2 slugs). `frontmatter.ts` is the deep, well-tested module (hand-rolled YAML-subset parser, replaced gray-matter for CVE-2026-59870) — the seam sits behind it.

**Plan must decide:** `normalizeContentDocument(raw) → ContentItem | ContentError` interface; error policy (surface error vs drop vs default); `prioritySlot` — emit it or remove it from the contract; `socialImage` — add to contract or remove from content files; fix the `Minimal Android Launcher.md` status or let the new error policy surface it; tests through the interface against the real content files.

## Candidate 3 — One shared content document + load module (Worth exploring)

**Finding:** The "frontmatter + body" shape is declared 3×: `ArticleData` in `ArticlePage.tsx:10-17` (standalone); `ArticleData extends ArticleSummary { body }` in `ArticlesPage.tsx:24-26`; `ContentData` + `isProjectData` guard in `ProjectPage.tsx`. Fetch boilerplate exists in 6 places with 3 divergent error policies: ArticlePage/ProjectPage 404→notFound; ArticlesPage has no 404 branch; HomeRecentPosts/HomeStartHere silently `setPosts([])`. `home-articles.ts` cross-feature imports `ArticleSummary` from `@/features/articles/articles-sidebar` and duplicates the `compareArticles` date sort.

**Plan must decide:** the single shape (which of the three wins); one error policy (404→notFound vs error object vs empty); module location (`front-end/src/shared/lib` vs the `shared` workspace package); the adapter seam (HTTP fetch in prod, in-memory in tests); migration order across the 6 consumers; what gets deleted (6 fetch copies, the cross-feature import, the duplicated sort).

## Candidate 4 — Give the home section a module (Worth exploring)

**Finding:** One section id is simultaneously the DOM id, URL hash, nav key, and observer key across 5 files (`config/home-sections.ts`, `HomeSection.tsx`, `HomeFloatingNav.tsx`, `useActiveHomeSection.ts`, `HomePage.tsx`). `HomeSection.tsx` branches on `section.id === 'start'` (line 153) and `ctaLabel?.toLowerCase() === 'discover'` (line 157); `HOME_NAV_ICONS` is a parallel registry; the `${section.id}-heading` convention is repeated in every branch; the section shell markup is copy-pasted across 5+ files.

**Plan must decide:** the variant set (which variants exist — start, cta/discover, default?); a single `sectionId(id)` seam so DOM id == hash == nav key == observer key; dispatch on the declared variant instead of string-matching id/label; the shell markup declared once; whether `HOME_NAV_ICONS` merges into the config.

## Candidate 5 — Concentrate content asset serving (Speculative)

**Finding:** `IMAGE_EXTENSIONS` (`back-end/src/features/content/obsidian.ts:1`) duplicates the keys of `IMAGE_MIME_TYPES` (`content-routes.ts:10-18`). The image route's path-traversal guard `isPathInsideRoot` (`content-routes.ts:20-23`) + MIME mapping + cache headers are untested through HTTP — `routes.test.ts` covers only /health, /hello, /, security headers, rate limiting.

**Plan must decide:** the `resolveAsset · serveAsset` interface; where the extension + MIME invariant lives (one list, one map — or one derived from the other); how the traversal guard is tested through the HTTP seam (filesystem/in-memory adapter); what the cache-header policy is.

## Notes

- Candidate 1 and 3 overlap on the article shape; plan them so 1's `renderArticle` consumes 3's shared shape, or sequence them.
- Candidate 2 and 5 are different seams of the same content pipeline (normalization vs asset serving); keep them separate.
- All plans must follow repo TDD rules: one failing test at a time, run the full suite after each change, never weaken existing tests.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 5 candidates has a plan with target interface, TDD steps, files changed/deleted, and tests written first; every open decision has a recommendation with rationale; plans follow repo TDD rules; no implementation code in this ticket.

title: chore(deploy): only replay kube pod when an image actually changed
description:
## Context
`deploy/systemd/website-update.timer` fires every 5 minutes and `website-update.service` then unconditionally runs `systemctl --user restart podman-kube@website.service` (#262). The `podman-kube@.service` template replays with `podman kube play --replace`, which tears down and recreates the pod containers on **every** invocation — including when `podman pull` returns "Image is up to date" and nothing changed.

Net effect: ~12 brief origin outages per hour (502s through the Cloudflare Tunnel) with zero benefit on the common no-new-image cycle. This is the literal "pull then replay" behaviour #262 specified; this issue tracks making the replay conditional.

## Decision
Restart/replay only when a pull actually changed an image. Candidate mechanisms (choose during implementation):

- **Digest compare** — record `podman image inspect --format '{{.Digest}}' <ref>` before and after each pull; restart only if either digest changed. Needs persistent state between executions (a marker file on the host, or a small helper script).
- **`podman kube apply`** — podman 5.x's diff-aware counterpart to `play --replace`: only recreates objects whose definition changed. Either call it directly or gate the existing restart on it.

## Scope
- `deploy/systemd/website-update.service` (timer schedule unchanged).
- Possibly a small helper script invoked by the unit to compare digests.
- Update `test/shared/src/deploy-config.test.ts` if the unit changes shape.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] When no image changed, the pod is NOT restarted (no gratuitous downtime).
- [ ] When a new `:latest` exists, the pod is replayed and the new version takes effect.
- [ ] Rollback via `podman pull :<git-sha>` + manual replay still documented and working.

## Dependencies
Builds on #262's units. No other dependencies.
